+# Use relative date filters in adaptive scopes | Microsoft Learn
+
+Relative date filters let you define [adaptive scope](purview-adaptive-scopes) membership by a date relative to the time of evaluation. For example, you can target recently created mailboxes, groups that are more than a year old, or sites whose project completion date falls within the past six months.
+
+Unlike a fixed date, a relative date moves forward without requiring you to edit the query. Use a relative date when you need a rolling range. Keep a fixed date when you need a cohort tied to a specific event, such as all sites created before a migration.
+
+Important
+
+Relative date filters determine which users, groups, or sites belong to a scope. They don't filter individual messages or documents by age, set a retention period, or change when retention starts. Configure those settings separately in the policy that uses the scope.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+You need the permissions and prerequisites for [configuring adaptive scopes](purview-adaptive-scopes#how-to-configure-an-adaptive-scope).
+
+Use the **Advanced query builder** to enter relative date filters. Use OPATH syntax for **Users** and **Microsoft 365 Groups**, and Keyword Query Language (KeyQL) syntax for **SharePoint sites**.
+
+For a custom SharePoint date property, work with your SharePoint administrator to populate the site metadata and map its crawled property to a supported date managed property. The property must represent a date for the site, not a date on an individual document. For background on custom site properties, see [Using Custom SharePoint Site Properties to Apply Microsoft 365 Retention with Adaptive Policy Scopes](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/security-compliance-and-identity/using-custom-sharepoint-site-properties-to-apply-microsoft-365/ba-p/3133970).
+
+## Supported date properties
+
+### Users and Microsoft 365 Groups
+
+| Property | Date used by the filter |
+| --- | --- |
+| `WhenCreated` | Creation date of the recipient object. |
+| `WhenCreatedUTC` | Creation date of the recipient object, expressed in UTC. |
+| `WhenMailboxCreated` | Creation date of the mailbox. This can differ from the creation date of the recipient object. |
+| `WhenChanged` | Last modification date of the recipient object. |
+| `WhenChangedUTC` | Last modification date of the recipient object, expressed in UTC. |
+| `WhenSoftDeleted` | Date the recipient was soft-deleted, when that value is present. |
+
+`WhenChanged` and `WhenChangedUTC` describe changes to the recipient object. They aren't measures of a person's last sign-in or mailbox activity.
+
+A filter on `WhenSoftDeleted` doesn't by itself make a deleted recipient eligible for scope membership. The recipient must also meet the scope's other membership requirements.
+
+For information about recipient properties, see [Filterable properties for recipient filters](/en-us/powershell/exchange/recipientfilter-properties).
+
+### SharePoint sites
+
+| Property | Date used by the filter |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Created` | Site creation date. |
+| `RefinableDate00` through `RefinableDate19` | Custom site dates mapped to these date managed properties, such as a project completion date. |
+
+Use the managed property name in the query, such as `RefinableDate00`. A date stored as text in a property such as `RefinableString00` isn't a supported relative date property.
+
+## Specify a relative date
+
+Use a date-only ISO 8601 duration. The value starts with an uppercase `P`, followed by a whole number and a unit:
+
+| Unit | Meaning | Example |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `Y` | Calendar years | `P1Y`: one year before evaluation. |
+| `M` | Calendar months | `P6M`: six months before evaluation. |
+| `W` | Weeks of seven days | `P2W`: 14 days before evaluation. |
+| `D` | Days | `P30D`: 30 days before evaluation. |
+
+You can combine years, months, and days in that order. For example, `P1Y6M` means one year and six months before evaluation, and `P1Y2M3D` means one year, two months, and three days before evaluation. Use weeks on their own, such as `P2W`, not `P1W3D`.
+
+`P0D` represents the evaluation time. It can provide an upper bound when you want to exclude future dates.
+
+Use uppercase letters and whole, nonnegative numbers. Time components, such as `PT2H` or `P1DT12H`, fractional values, negative values, and expressions such as `30 days` aren't supported.
+
+### How the cutoff date is calculated
+
+The cutoff date moves forward every day, so the scope continues to use the same rolling date range without you changing the query. For example, if the current date is November 1, 2026, `P30D` represents October 2, 2026. On November 2, 2026, it represents October 3, 2026. Scope membership changes dynamically as users, groups, or sites fall inside or outside the query's date range.
+
+Relative dates use UTC. These examples show dates only, but the cutoff includes a time of day rather than always starting at midnight.
+
+Months and years follow the calendar, rather than fixed numbers of days. For example, `P1M` isn't always equivalent to `P30D`. When a target month doesn't have the original day, the cutoff falls on the last valid day of that month.
+
+### Choose a comparison operator
+
+The comparison applies to the property's date, not to its age:
+
+| Meaning | OPATH operator | KeyQL operator |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Later than the cutoff, more recent | `-gt` | `>` |
+| On or after the cutoff | `-ge` | `>=` |
+| Earlier than the cutoff, older | `-lt` | `<` |
+| On or before the cutoff | `-le` | `<=` |
+
+For example, `WhenMailboxCreated -ge 'P30D'` matches creation dates on or after the rolling 30-day cutoff. To match mailboxes older than 30 days, use `WhenMailboxCreated -lt 'P30D'`.
+
+Don't use equality or inequality operators with relative dates: OPATH `-eq` and `-ne`, or KeyQL `=`, `:`, and `<>`. To express a range, combine two comparisons with `-and` in OPATH or `AND` in KeyQL. Relative date ranges using KeyQL `..` syntax aren't supported.
+
+Enclose OPATH duration values in single or double quotes. For KeyQL, use double quotes, as in `Created>="P30D"`, or leave the duration unquoted, as in `Created>=P30D`. The following examples use quoted values.
+
+## Create an adaptive scope with a relative date filter
+
+1. In the [Microsoft Purview portal](https://purview.microsoft.com/), go to **Settings** > **Roles and scopes** > **Adaptive scopes**, and select **+ Create scope**.
+2. Follow the prompts to name the scope and select an administrative unit or **Full directory**. SharePoint site scopes require **Full directory**.
+3. Select **Users**, **Microsoft 365 Groups**, or **SharePoint sites**.
+4. Select **Advanced query builder** and enter a query that uses the appropriate syntax and a supported date property. Use the examples in the next section as starting points.
+5. Review and create the scope. Allow time for evaluation, then check its membership before adding it to a policy.
+
+You can also pass the query to the **RawQuery** parameter of [New-AdaptiveScope](/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-adaptivescope) or [Set-AdaptiveScope](/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-adaptivescope) in [Security & Compliance PowerShell](/en-us/powershell/exchange/connect-to-scc-powershell).
+
+## Examples
+
+These examples define scope membership only. Choose the policy settings separately for your organization's requirements.
+
+### Recently created mailboxes
+
+To create a **Users** scope for mailboxes created on or after the rolling 30-day cutoff:
+
+```text
+WhenMailboxCreated -ge 'P30D'
+```
+
+You can combine the date filter with other supported conditions. For example, to restrict the same scope to recipients in the Finance department:
+
+```text
+(Department -eq 'Finance') -and (WhenMailboxCreated -ge 'P30D')
+```
+
+As the cutoff moves forward, mailboxes older than the cutoff no longer match.
+
+### Groups older than one year
+
+To create a **Microsoft 365 Groups** scope for groups whose recipient objects were created more than one year before evaluation:
+
+```text
+WhenCreatedUTC -lt 'P1Y'
+```
+
+This is an age-based scope. It doesn't identify groups that have been unused for a year.
+
+### Recipient objects between one and two years old
+
+To create a **Users** scope for recipient objects created on or after the two-year cutoff but before the one-year cutoff:
+
+```text
+(WhenCreatedUTC -ge 'P2Y') -and (WhenCreatedUTC -lt 'P1Y')
+```
+
+The older cutoff is the lower date bound. Reversing these comparisons would produce an empty range.
+
+### SharePoint sites older than two years
+
+To create a **SharePoint sites** scope for sites created more than two years before evaluation:
+
+```text
+Created<"P2Y"
+```
+
+You can also combine a relative date with other site conditions. For example, to include only modern communication sites created after the six-month cutoff:
+
+```text
+SiteTemplate=SITEPAGEPUBLISHING AND Created>"P6M"
+```
+
+### Project sites completed within the past six months
+
+Suppose your SharePoint administrator has mapped each project's completion date to `RefinableDate00`. To create a **SharePoint sites** scope for completion dates from six months before evaluation through the evaluation time:
+
+```text
+RefinableDate00>="P6M" AND RefinableDate00<="P0D"
+```
+
+The upper bound excludes planned completion dates in the future. Verify the mapping and populated values before using this query.
+
+## Validate relative date filters
+
+After creating or updating a scope, use [View adaptive scope membership details](purview-adaptive-scopes#view-adaptive-scope-membership-details) to review added and removed members. You can also use [Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers](/en-us/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-adaptivescopemembers).
+
+Adaptive scopes are evaluated periodically, not continuously. Initial membership and membership changes can take up to five days to appear. A recipient or site doesn't enter or leave the displayed member list immediately when it crosses a date cutoff.
+
+### Test a query outside adaptive scopes
+
+Exchange PowerShell filters and SharePoint search don't perform the adaptive scope conversion of ISO 8601 duration values. To [validate an advanced query independently](purview-adaptive-scopes#validate-advanced-queries), replace each duration with an absolute UTC date calculated from one reference time.
+
+For example, after [connecting to Exchange Online PowerShell](/en-us/powershell/exchange/connect-to-exchange-online-powershell), you can check the user mailbox portion of the recently created mailboxes example:
+
+```powershell
+$referenceTime = [DateTime]::UtcNow
+$cutoff = $referenceTime.AddDays(-30).ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ", [Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture)
+Get-Mailbox -RecipientTypeDetails UserMailbox -Filter "WhenMailboxCreated -ge '$cutoff'" -ResultSize Unlimited
+```
+
+For SharePoint search, use the same approach. For example, at reference time `2026-11-23T12:00:00Z`, test `Created<"P2Y"` by using `Created<"2024-11-23T12:00:00Z"`.
+
+These checks test the property values and query at the chosen time. They don't force an adaptive scope evaluation or guarantee identical membership results. The adaptive scope can evaluate later, and its other membership requirements still apply.
+
+### Troubleshoot unexpected results
+
+| Symptom | What to check |
+| --- | --- |
+| The query isn't accepted. | Check the scope type, property name, duration format, and comparison operator. Use the advanced query builder, quote OPATH values, and avoid time components and equality operators. |
+| Recent objects match when you expected older objects, or the reverse. | Use `<` or `-lt` for dates older than the cutoff, and `>` or `-gt` for dates more recent than the cutoff. Use the inclusive forms when required. |
+| A custom site date doesn't produce the expected matches. | Confirm that the site metadata is populated and mapped to the intended `RefinableDate` managed property. |
+| A mailbox doesn't match a recipient creation-date filter. | Compare `WhenCreated` or `WhenCreatedUTC` with `WhenMailboxCreated`. Recipient and mailbox creation dates can differ. |
+| Membership hasn't changed after a date boundary passes. | Allow time for the next evaluation and for membership details to update. |
\ No newline at end of file

englishSummary.headline: Relative date filters documented for adaptive scopes
englishSummary.summary: A new article explains how to use rolling date filters for users, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites, including supported properties, query syntax, and custom SharePoint date prerequisites.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators can create adaptive scopes based on changing date ranges. Custom SharePoint dates require site metadata and managed-property mapping; retention settings remain configured separately.

+Permanent deletion can override retention settings or eDiscovery holds. Deleting items subject to legal holds requires explicit administrator approval for disposition. Items already copied to an eDiscovery review set aren't deleted by Priority Cleanup.
+
+## Understand permanent deletion and recovery limitations
+
+When an administrator selects **Delete data permanently**, they request permanent deletion of the targeted SharePoint and OneDrive content. Deleted content bypasses the recycle bins and isn't recoverable under ordinary circumstances. Review the consequences before you configure and approve permanent deletion.
+
+After permanent deletion, Microsoft can retain a protected copy of the deleted content for up to 90 days. This copy is kept solely to handle exceptional privacy or security incidents involving permanent deletion. Customers, including users and administrators, can't access the copy. The copy isn't available through SharePoint search or eDiscovery.
+
+In an exceptional scenario, customers can submit a support ticket to request recovery. Recovery is subject to Microsoft review and approval and is attempted only on a best-effort basis. Recovery isn't guaranteed. The temporary retention of deleted content doesn't provide a customer-accessible recovery option.
+
+For general Microsoft 365 data-handling policies, see [Data retention, deletion, and destruction in Microsoft 365](/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-data-retention-deletion-and-destruction-overview).
+
+This recovery information applies to SharePoint and OneDrive. For mailbox cleanup, see [Use priority cleanup to expedite the permanent deletion of sensitive information from mailboxes](priority-cleanup-exchange).
 
 ## Configure permanent deletion

+
+- If the policy and library default specify the same sensitivity label, the expected label remains that label. This doesn't guarantee that no labeling operations or transient failures occur.
+- If they specify different labels, the policy can replace a lower-priority automatically applied or default label, including a library default. The library default doesn't replace a higher-priority label or any manually applied label.
+- By default, the policy also preserves manually applied labels. Replacing a lower-priority manual label requires the policy's explicit override setting; this option doesn't change the library default's behavior. See [Will an existing label be overridden?](apply-sensitivity-label-automatically#will-an-existing-label-be-overridden).
+
+For failures reported by an auto-labeling policy, see [Resolve auto-labeling failures in SharePoint and OneDrive files](/en-us/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/purview/sensitivity-labels/auto-labeling-failures-sharepoint-onedrive#resolve-auto-labeling-failures). The portal's **Conflict** code indicates a concurrent version or save conflict and is retried automatically. **CannotOverrideCurrentLabel** indicates that an existing label has equal or higher priority; the existing label takes precedence.
+
 ## Requirements
 
+- An eligible premium subscription for library default labeling. Check the **Apply default sensitivity labeling for SharePoint Document library** entry in the [Microsoft Purview sensitivity labeling licensing requirements](/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-information-protection-sensitivity-labeling), including the applicable prerequisite licenses. Manual labeling entitlement alone doesn't establish entitlement to this feature.
 - You've [created and published](create-sensitivity-labels) sensitivity labels that include the [label scope](sensitivity-labels#label-scopes) of **Files & other data assets** and these labels are published to the users who will select a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library.
 - You've [enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive](sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files). To check this status, you can run `(Get-SPOTenant).EnableAIPIntegration` from the [SharePoint Online Management Shell](/en-us/powershell/sharepoint/sharepoint-online/connect-sharepoint-online) to confirm the value is set to **True**.
 - To support sensitivity labels for PDFs, you've [added support for PDFs in SharePoint](sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files#adding-support-for-pdf). To check this status, you can run `(Get-SPOTenant).EnableSensitivityLabelforPDF` from the [SharePoint Online Management Shell](/en-us/powershell/sharepoint/sharepoint-online/connect-sharepoint-online) to confirm the value is set to **True**.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview: Archive SharePoint files under retention policies
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management will enable admins to archive inactive SharePoint files under retention policies starting mid-January 2027. Archived files move to Microsoft 365 Archive, remain compliant and discoverable, and are excluded from Copilot indexing to improve response relevance. Admin configuration is required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

What and why 

Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management now allows admins to archive SharePoint files based on retention policies. This helps organizations reduce storage costs by moving inactive content to Microsoft 365 Archive while maintaining compliance and discoverability. Archived content is excluded from Copilot indexing, which can improve the relevance of Copilot responses by focusing results on current, active data.

Rollout schedule 

General Availability (GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026) and expected to complete by mid-February 2027 (previously early January)

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Admins managing Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
  • Organizations using retention policies in SharePoint Online and OneDrive

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview (Data Lifecycle Management)
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft 365 Archive
  • Microsoft Copilot

What will happen

  • A new Archive option will be available within retention policy settings in Data Lifecycle Management.
  • Admins can configure retention policies to move inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive storage.
  • Archived files remain available for compliance scenarios, including eDiscovery.
  • Archived content will be excluded from Copilot indexing, helping improve answer relevance.
  • This feature is not enabled by default and requires admin configuration.
  • Existing retention policies and compliance configurations remain unchanged unless updated by admins.

Action required and recommendations

No immediate action is required. To prepare for and take advantage of this feature, we recommend that you:

  • Review your current retention policies in Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management.
  • Evaluate opportunities to reduce storage costs by archiving inactive content.
  • Update retention policies to include the new Archive option where appropriate.
  • Inform compliance and records management stakeholders about this new capability.
  • Review internal documentation and processes related to data lifecycle and storage optimization.

Learn more: Configure Microsoft 365 retention settings to automatically retain or delete content | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data, and if so where, is it cached or permanently stored?Files moved by retention policies are relocated to Microsoft 365 Archive storage, a distinct storage tier, and are stored there until restored or otherwise actioned.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Archived files move out of active storage into Microsoft 365 Archive, changing how those files are stored and accessed going forward.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Archived content is excluded from Copilot indexing, which changes what data Copilot can access and surface in responses.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable Purview capabilities such as retention policies, holds, or eDiscovery?Retention policies gain a new archive action, and archived files remain subject to eDiscovery, extending existing retention and discovery workflows.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Data Lifecycle Management - Archive SharePoint files under retention
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management will add an Archive option to retention policies, allowing admins to move inactive SharePoint files to Microsoft 365 Archive for cost savings while maintaining compliance and discoverability. Archived content is excluded from Copilot indexing. Rollout begins September 2026; admin configuration is required.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

What and Why

Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management is introducing the ability to archive SharePoint files based on retention policies. This feature helps organizations reduce storage costs by moving inactive content to Microsoft 365 Archive while maintaining compliance and discoverability. By excluding archived content from Copilot indexing, organizations can also improve the relevance and quality of Copilot responses, ensuring users focus on current, active data.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 561208.

Rollout Schedule

Public Preview: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 (previously mid-August) and expect to complete by early October 2026 (previously early September).

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and is expected to complete by early January 2027 (previously early December 2026).

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected

  • Admins managing Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
  • Organizations using retention policies in SharePoint Online and OneDrive

Platforms/ServicesPlatforms/Services

  • Microsoft Purview (Data Lifecycle Management)
  • SharePoint Online
  • Microsoft 365 Archive
  • Microsoft Copilot

What will happen

  • A new Archive option will be available within retention policy settings in Data Lifecycle Management.
  • Admins can configure retention policies to move inactive files to Microsoft 365 Archive storage.
  • Archived files remain available for compliance scenarios, including eDiscovery.
  • Archived content will be excluded from Copilot indexing, helping improve answer relevance.
  • This feature is not enabled by default and requires admin configuration.
  • Existing retention policies and compliance configurations remain unchanged unless updated by admins.

Action Required / Recommendations

No immediate action is required.

To prepare and take advantage of this feature:

  • Review your current retention policies in Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management.
  • Evaluate opportunities to reduce storage costs by archiving inactive content.
  • Update retention policies to include the new Archive option where appropriate.
  • Inform compliance and records management stakeholders about this new capability.
  • Review internal documentation and processes related to data lifecycle and storage optimization.

Compliance Considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. Archived files are stored in Microsoft 365 Archive (low-cost storage tier).
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Files meeting retention criteria can be moved from active storage to archive storage while remaining discoverable.
Does the change introduce or modify AI/ML capabilities interacting with data?Yes. Archived content is excluded from Copilot indexing, influencing how Copilot processes and retrieves organizational data.
Does the change modify Purview retention policies or workflows?Yes. Adds a new Archive action within retention policy configuration in Data Lifecycle Management.
Does the change affect eDiscovery or Content Search?Yes. Archived content remains discoverable for compliance workflows such as eDiscovery.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins configure and enable the feature through retention policy settings in Purview.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Data Lifecycle Management - Hard delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with priority cleanup workflow
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview introduces a priority cleanup workflow allowing admins to hard delete specific OneDrive and SharePoint content, overriding retention policies with eDiscovery admin approval. Rolling out mid-August 2026 (preview) and early December 2026 (general availability), this feature requires explicit admin setup and supports compliance oversight.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

We are introducing a new priority cleanup workflow in Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management that allows administrators to permanently delete (hard delete) specific OneDrive and SharePoint content types, even when retention policies or holds are in place. This capability helps reduce data exposure risk from rapidly growing Copilot-related content while maintaining compliance through required eDiscovery admin review and approval.

This change is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558343.

When this will happen:

Public Preview: We will begin rolling out mid-August 2026 (previously mid-July) and expect to complete by early December 2026 (previously end of November).

General Availability (Worldwide) Rollout begins early December 2026 (previously end of November) and is expected to complete by mid-January 2027 (previously early January).

How this affects your organization:

Who is affected:

  • Microsoft 365 administrators managing Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management
  • Organizations using OneDrive for Business and SharePoint Online with retention policies or holds

What will happen:

  • Admins can create a priority cleanup policy targeting specific content types in OneDrive and SharePoint.
  • A new Delete data permanently option enables hard deletion of targeted items.
  • Content deleted through this workflow is fully removed and is no longer discoverable in:
    • SharePoint search
    • Copilot experiences
    • eDiscovery (after required approval)
  • For content under hold, eDiscovery admin review and approval is required before deletion.
  • This capability is not enabled by default and requires explicit admin configuration.
  • There is no change to user workflows unless an admin configures and applies a priority cleanup policy.

What you can do to prepare:

  • Review your organization’s data risk and retention strategy, especially for Copilot-generated content such as Teams transcripts.
  • In Microsoft Purview, plan and configure a priority cleanup policy if permanent deletion is required for specific content types:
    • Navigate to Microsoft Purview portal > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup.
    • Create a new policy and select Delete data permanently in the policy settings.
  • Ensure appropriate eDiscovery admin roles and approval processes are in place for content under hold.
  • Update internal governance or compliance documentation to reflect this new deletion capability.

Learn more: Compare types of groups in Microsoft 365 - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations:

Compliance areaExplanation
Alteration of existing customer data processingThis change introduces a priority cleanup workflow that allows permanent deletion of specific OneDrive and SharePoint content types, even when retention policies or holds exist, subject to required approval.
eDiscovery or Content SearchContent deleted through the priority cleanup workflow is fully removed and no longer discoverable in eDiscovery or Content Search after eDiscovery admin review and approval for items under hold.
Retention policies, holds, or deletion workflowsAdds a new admin-controlled deletion workflow that can override standard retention outcomes through an approved hard-delete process.
Admin controls and compliance monitoringThe feature is managed by administrators in Microsoft Purview and includes review and approval steps that support compliance oversight and auditing.
